dimension_justifications.soundness: The conditional, receipt-level claims are carefully scoped and supported by a coherent 2x2 ownership factorial, lifecycle witnesses, selected independent numerical checks, and matched live faults (Sections 3-5; Figure 3; Tables 5, 7, 15, and 17). However, the paper itself reports incomplete terminal source-tree closure and cannot independently recapture the producer; selected operator oracles also do not cover upstream activation construction or end-to-end semantics (Section 6; Section 7; Appendix I). These are substantive limitations, but they do not invalidate the explicitly conditional audit result.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Excellent. The paper cleanly separates the contract, experimental scope, claim authorization, and limitations. Figures 1-3 and Tables 4-5 make the intended evidentiary boundary unusually easy to assess, and the manuscript is visually polished. Some appendices are dense, but they remain readable and directly support verification.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The main contribution is a useful integration of known testing, provenance, ownership, and memory-accounting ideas into a phase-aware receipt contract for hybrid KV/recurrent state. The paper positions this novelty candidly (Appendix Tables 9-10). Its significance is limited by validation on one frozen stack and sequential schedule, but the contract and evidence taxonomy should be useful to hybrid-serving implementers.

paper_summary: ForkAudit proposes a receipt-bound audit contract for safe forking of hybrid LLM state, distinguishing immutable document KV from mutable recurrent GDN state and separating logical, allocator, and service-capacity memory denominators. In a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B case study, it crosses full-copy versus shared-document KV with materialized versus borrowed GDN bases at N={1,8,32}; reports matching registered observables, storage-lifecycle predicates, selected dense-FP32/NumPy operator checks, live-fault gate reachability, and allocator deltas (Sections 3-5; Tables 5, 7, 15).
strongest_verified_contribution: A clearly specified, phase-aware ownership witness for hybrid state: borrowed GDN bases may alias only before first transition, after which request-local tensors must be disjoint from bases and peers, paired with explicit typed-record/replay obligations (Section 3; Figure 2; Appendix D).
strengths: It identifies an important systems distinction that output agreement alone cannot establish: request isolation and memory-denominator savings are separate claims (Introduction, pp. 1-2).

The primary factorial is well structured: 96 rank-fan-out-factor configurations, all four ownership cells, and 288 adjacent-fan-out comparisons are reported separately from contextual cohorts (Section 5.3; Table 4).

The authors are unusually disciplined about evidence scope: Figures 1 and 3, Table 5, and Section 6 explicitly distinguish conditional receipt replay, selected numerical support, positive controls, and non-claims about scheduling or capacity.
The paper includes constructive fault sensitivity rather than relying only on clean-run equivalence; Table 7 maps nine live injected faults to predeclared gates.

Memory reporting is appropriately denominator-aware: controlled pools, post-pack allocator peaks, and full-lifecycle peaks are distinguished instead of being conflated with NVML or admission capacity (Section 4.4; Table 6).
questions: Can the authors provide a terminally closed, independently reproducible source snapshot for the primary run, and explain precisely why the post-ledger pycache change cannot be excluded or incorporated without invalidating the original ledger?

What evidence would show that the ownership contract remains valid under concurrent kernels, ragged/continuous batching, scheduler cancellation, and a compiled-kernel/autotuning change rather than the recorded Python callable?
For the deployment-context F1 values in Table 2, please specify the eight workload instances, prompts, scoring details, per-workload results, and variability across the three timing repeats.

issues.location: Section 7, p. 8; Appendix Table 5, p. 13; Appendix J/Table 18, p. 21
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript states that post-ledger pycache files broke terminal code-tree closure, so frozen identity is only partial; it further states that receipt replay does not independently recapture the producer. Table 5 labels frozen identity partial, and Table 18 only points to an accompanying package.
issues.why_it_matters: For a paper whose central contribution is a receipt-bound audit, an unclosed executed source tree weakens the binding from the receipts to the exact candidate implementation. The claimed result remains meaningful under the stated honest-capture boundary, but outside readers cannot fully verify the stronger provenance premise from the described material.
issues.required_fix: Release a cryptographically closed, immutable executed source/environment snapshot or a documented reconstruction that proves equivalence to the pre-output bound tree; explicitly separate any claims that still depend on an unverified producer.
issues.verification_test: An independent party should reproduce the manifest bindings and replay from the released closed snapshot, with no untracked post-ledger files and with resulting receipt digests matching the registered aggregate.
issues.evidence_needed: A terminal source-tree manifest, environment/container digest, command provenance, and independent rerun/replay report.

issues.location: Sections 3.1 and 4.3, pp. 4-5; Sections 5.4-5.5, p. 7; Section 6, p. 8; Appendix I, p. 20
issues.observed_evidence: The attention oracle covers eight selected captured post-RoPE rows, while the GDN oracle covers four captured post-normalization transitions; the paper explicitly excludes upstream activation construction, q/k normalization, all GDN layers, compiled-binary identity, and end-to-end verification. Cross-cell equivalence is relational and therefore cannot independently rule out shared defects.
issues.why_it_matters: The tests substantiate selected ownership predicates and selected operators, but a systematic common-mode bug before the capture boundary or in an untested layer/schedule could preserve all registered cross-arm digests. This limits how strongly the audit can be interpreted as evidence of whole-model hybrid correctness.
issues.required_fix: Either narrow the headline claims further to receipt-level ownership only, or add independent end-to-end/reference checks across more layers, sequence geometries, and execution schedules, including an independently built implementation or recapture path.
issues.verification_test: Demonstrate agreement with an independent end-to-end reference over sampled full sequences and show detection of held-out upstream, layer, and scheduling faults not used to design the current gates.
issues.evidence_needed: Held-out fault campaign, broader operator coverage, and independent end-to-end comparisons spanning the omitted boundaries.

issues.location: Section 5.2 and Table 2, p. 6; Appendix I, p. 20
issues.observed_evidence: Table 2 reports medians over 24 measurements and an eight-workload mean F1, with only three timing repeats per configuration. Per-workload scores, dispersion, exact workload composition, and scoring details are not shown in the PDF.
issues.why_it_matters: The authors appropriately present this table as context rather than primary audit evidence, but aggregate values make it difficult to assess whether the reported quality/state tradeoff is robust or dominated by particular workloads.
issues.required_fix: Add per-workload outcomes, dispersion or raw trial summaries, exact evaluation prompts/scoring, and a clearer distinction between timing repetitions and independent workload units.
issues.verification_test: Recompute Table 2 from disclosed per-workload results and verify that the reported ranking and caveated Q16 interpretation persist across workloads.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-workload F1 and latency records plus evaluation protocol details.

ethics_concerns: No material ethics issue is apparent from the manuscript. The paper includes an ethics statement and acknowledges that memory efficiency may scale deployment; its use of PG-19 training text and systems measurements does not introduce a specific unaddressed human-subject or deployment claim (Appendix A, p. 12).
llm_usage_disclosure: This internal review was produced with LLM assistance from the frozen PDF-only snapshot. It did not inspect source code, artifacts, prior reviews, external web sources, or other repository materials.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A closed executed-source and environment snapshot independently replayed by a third party.
Independent end-to-end validation and held-out fault testing beyond the current selected captured-input boundaries.
Demonstrations across concurrent/ragged scheduling, additional hybrid models, page sizes, and state precisions.
Per-workload deployment-context results with reproducible evaluation and uncertainty reporting.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Failure to reconcile the final source tree with the pre-output ledger or a replay mismatch under a closed snapshot.
A held-out common-mode, upstream, or scheduler fault that passes the current receipts while violating isolation or semantics.
Per-workload deployment results showing that the reported F1/state tradeoff is not robust.
review_limitations: This was a PDF-only review; I did not execute or inspect the referenced accompanying artifacts.
Assessment of cited prior work and artifact availability is limited to what the manuscript states.
